text_blocks.snippet: The recommended duration of Prolia (denosumab) treatment for osteoporosis is generally long-term, potentially lifelong, but this depends on individual risk factors and response to treatment. While clinical trials often last 3-5 years, ongoing research suggests benefits for up to 10 years or even longer, especially for those at high risk. However, discontinuing Prolia can lead to a rapid decrease in bone density and increased fracture risk, so careful consideration and planning are needed if stopping treatment.
